-- 143_quantity_kinds.sql
-- SCHEMA migration (T-020; no data rows beyond the six-kind seed of the vocabulary table). A parameter states what
-- kind of quantity it is, and on what evidence anyone judged that it is one.
--
-- WHY. An element such as a grab bar can be promoted to a parameter: it then owes a reading from every source and is
-- determined as a cell, though it measures nothing, and nothing on the row says what it measures. Whether a term names
-- an element or a quantity cannot be computed from the term; it is a judgment (CLAUDE.md rule 8), so the writer asks
-- for it, constrained to the live vocabulary, and records the answer and its warrant in named columns. OD-24 (delegated
-- resolution 2026-11-12 in references/project-standards.md): a parameter states a quantity kind from a table of kinds
-- held as rows and extended by data with a warrant, not a CHECK list.
--
-- WHAT. base_quantity_kinds: one row per kind, its definition, and the dated ledger heading that admitted it (the
-- pointer terms.catalogue_approval_ref uses). Two nullable columns on base_parameters: the kind, and the observation
-- (observed_terms) whose verbatim quote states a value of the quantity, which is the warrant, a pointer and not a copy.
-- Nullable because the live parameters take their kind in a research pull request (T-109); db.py add-parameter
-- enforces both for every new row. A CHECK naming both columns is not added: the writer holds it.
--
-- SEED. Exactly the kinds OD-24 lists, each admitted by that entry. Ratio, percentage and degrees are notations of
-- gradient (T-030's), not kinds. created_at is the date of writing.
--
-- WHAT READS IT. db.py add-parameter (reads base_quantity_kinds and observed_terms), db.py add-quantity-kind (writes).

CREATE TABLE base_quantity_kinds (
    kind_id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(trim(kind_id)) > 0),
    definition          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(definition)) > 0),
    approval_ref        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(approval_ref)) > 0),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT
);

INSERT INTO base_quantity_kinds (kind_id, definition, approval_ref, created_at, created_by_session) VALUES
 ('length', 'A distance measured along a straight line between two points of a room, a route or a fitting.',
  'Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-24 how coarse a parameter is, and its quantity kinds', '$D 00:00', 'migration_143'),
 ('gradient', 'The rise of a surface over its run; a ratio, a percentage and an angle in degrees are notations of this one kind, not kinds of their own.',
  'Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-24 how coarse a parameter is, and its quantity kinds', '$D 00:00', 'migration_143'),
 ('force', 'A push, pull or turn that a person must apply to operate or move something.',
  'Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-24 how coarse a parameter is, and its quantity kinds', '$D 00:00', 'migration_143'),
 ('time', 'A duration, such as how long a sound takes to decay or a door stays open.',
  'Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-24 how coarse a parameter is, and its quantity kinds', '$D 00:00', 'migration_143'),
 ('luminous_reflectance', 'The share of incident light a surface reflects (light reflectance value, LRV), and the contrast between two surfaces stated as the difference of their LRVs on that same scale.',
  'Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-24 how coarse a parameter is, and its quantity kinds', '$D 00:00', 'migration_143'),
 ('colour_temperature', 'The correlated colour temperature of a white light source, on the warm-to-cool scale.',
  'Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-24 how coarse a parameter is, and its quantity kinds', '$D 00:00', 'migration_143');

ALTER TABLE base_parameters ADD COLUMN quantity_kind TEXT REFERENCES base_quantity_kinds(kind_id);
ALTER TABLE base_parameters ADD COLUMN quantity_kind_observation_id INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id);

PRAGMA user_version = 143;
EOF

def insert_quantity_kind(kind_id: str, definition: str, approval_ref: str, session: str,
                         dry_run: bool = False):
    """Admit a quantity kind to `base_quantity_kinds` (T-020, OD-24): a kind is added by data, on a ledger pointer.

    Refuses a blank session, an id that is not lower-case letters and underscores with a letter first, a definition
    holding a digit (a kind is not a value), an `--approval-ref` that is not exactly one dated `## ` heading of the
    ledger (`dbcore.require_approval_heading`, the lookup `mint-term-from-catalogue` uses), and an existing kind.
    What stays unproved is that the entry approves THIS kind: the operator answers for the match.
    """
    kind_id, definition = (kind_id or "").strip(), (definition or "").strip()
    if not (session or "").strip():
        raise Refusal("add-quantity-kind: --session is required and may not be blank.")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z_]*", kind_id):
        raise Refusal(f"add-quantity-kind: --kind-id {kind_id!r} must be lower-case letters and underscores, "
                      f"a letter first (the shape of the seeded kinds).")
    if not definition or any(ch.isdigit() for ch in definition):
        raise Refusal(f"add-quantity-kind: --definition {definition!r} must be present and carry no digit: a kind "
                      f"names a quantity, never a value.")
    approval_ref = dbcore.require_approval_heading(approval_ref, "add-quantity-kind")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        held = conn.execute("SELECT kind_id, approval_ref FROM base_quantity_kinds WHERE kind_id=?",
                            [kind_id]).fetchone()
        if held:
            raise Refusal(f"add-quantity-kind: {kind_id!r} is already a kind (admitted by "
                          f"{held['approval_ref']!r}). Nothing was written.")
        row = {"kind_id": kind_id, "definition": definition, "approval_ref": approval_ref}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "base_quantity_kinds", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO base_quantity_kinds ({','.join(row)}) "
                     f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        return {"kind_id": kind_id, "approval_ref": approval_ref, "dry_run": dry_run}

-- 145_retire_admissions_and_connections_in_place.sql
-- SCHEMA migration (T-050; OD-29, resolved under delegation: a connection and a search-to-source admission edge are
-- data rows under the owner's ruling of 2026-09-16, "RETIRE IN PLACE, NEVER HARD-DELETE"; a genuine deletion of either
-- is an exception only the owner rules on). No data rows.
--
-- `search_admissions` and `connections` each gain the retirement shape `specifications` and `extraction_lens_links`
-- already use: `retired_at`, `retired_by_session` and `retirement_reason`, nullable, set together or not at all. The
-- CHECK sits on the last of the three, because SQLite adds a column by ALTER and a column constraint may name its
-- siblings. `connection_targets` gains nothing: a target of a retired connection is retired through its pointer.
--
-- THE RULING'S EXECUTION CONDITION: "No row is retired in place until every reader that could surface it filters on
-- status." The two views that read `search_admissions` filter below; every other reader of either table is a script and
-- is fixed in the same pull request (db.py, research_batch_dod.py, test_db_integrity.py, graph/extract_db.py).
--  * v_source_admission, from its current text in sqlite_master (migration 070 set it), gains `AND sa.retired_at IS NULL`:
--    a withdrawn attribution is not "the search that admitted this source".
--  * v_coverage_parameter_via_admission, from its current text (migration 140 set it), gains the same predicate in the
--    `reached` CTE: a search does not reach a parameter through an admission it has withdrawn. No view reads
--    `connections` or `connection_targets`.
-- The retired edge stays a row: it is the record that the claim was made, when, by whom and why it was withdrawn, and it
-- is never un-retired in place (db.py link-admission refuses it and names log-search).
-- WRITERS: db.py unlink-admission and delete-connection (each now sets the three columns instead of deleting).
-- READERS: the two views above, db.py get_connections, db.py's parameter reach, research_batch_dod R17,
-- test_db_integrity S01 and the graph extractor.

ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retirement_reason TEXT
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL));

ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retirement_reason TEXT
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL));

DROP VIEW v_source_admission;
CREATE VIEW v_source_admission AS
SELECT
    es.ref_id,
    es.pub_title,
    es.tier                     AS source_tier,
    es.evidence_type,
    es.verification_status,
    es.verification_disposition,
    se.exec_id,
    se.slug                     AS admitted_under_slug,
    se.query_text,
    se.engine,
    se.language,
    se.jurisdiction             AS search_jurisdiction,
    se.depth_method,
    se.mining_direction,
    se.target_tier,
    se.backfill                 AS search_was_backfilled,
    se.created_by_session                  AS admitting_session,
    se.created_at              AS admitted_at,
    -- The research-stage prior, reached by pointer rather than copied onto the
    -- evidence row. This is what makes CHECK 7 answerable.
    se.prior_expectation
FROM evidence_sources es
